tasks.short: Shape musical performance through gestures conveying tempo, phrasing, tone and volume changes.

steps.what: Listen to the actual ensemble and decide the desired expressive adjustment
Use gestures to communicate tempo, phrasing, tone, pitch, volume and musical colour
outputs: actual gestural direction and musical response

steps.what: Write and check any actual expressive markings needed for later direction
inputs: actual gestural direction and musical response

steps.what: Save the approved final score annotations

tasks.design: Retain listening, expressive choice and physical gestures. OTHER denotes the existing {DIGITAL_SCORE} annotation tool. Annotation writing and its approved save are separated. Existing direct annotation and native score navigation offer no additional change for this live gestural task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Expressive gestures depend on the live musical moment.
tasks.enabler_now: Current score tools already retain markings; no new reduction is established.
tasks.still_hard: Shaping an ensembles response through precise embodied communication.
tasks.human_edge: The director hears and communicates a musical intention in the moment.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: live conducting depends on listening and physical gestures; existing digital annotations can preserve decisions but do not perform that work.

assumptions: Provisional allocation includes separated annotation writing and save rather than excluding them. Native templates and score views were assessed; the assumed existing direct annotation route has no repeated transcription to remove.
s3 captures actual bar_reference and expressive_marking at full time after the gesture/response. No new system or ongoing upkeep is introduced. The save remains fully retained and earns no benefit.
unknowns: Whether actual markings are duplicated across score systems
research_questions: Is any expressive marking re-keyed after being entered in the existing score?

incremental.description: No new tool or maintenance; existing direction and annotation retained

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Listening, physical gestures, separated actual markings and same-system save all remain at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct rehearsals and performances toward intended musical effects.

steps.what: Locate the current score, parts and marked rehearsal passages in the native score view
inputs: existing bar references and rehearsal marks

steps.what: Direct rehearsal and performance, listening and adjusting balance, volume changes, rhythm and tempo
outputs: actual musical performance and director observations

steps.what: Write and approve actual rehearsal observations and precise score markings
inputs: actual musical performance and director observations

steps.what: Save the approved final rehearsal annotations

tasks.design: Configure native bookmarks and current-part links in {DIGITAL_SCORE}, denoted OTHER. Retrieve existing passages faster while retaining all rehearsal and performance direction. Actual notes and their same-system save remain fully retained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating marked passages across score and parts may require repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native score bookmarks and linked parts can reduce navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Listening, balancing the ensemble and shaping the performance.
tasks.human_edge: The director hears the whole and helps musicians respond together.
tasks.altitude: Live musical leadership with easier score retrieval.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native digital score bookmarks can retrieve existing marked passages and parts.

assumptions: Provisional shares require actual observation of remaining passage navigation. Existing native links receive no new saving.

Current score files and bar/part identifiers already exist from the music publisher or director. s1 retains edition, part and bar checks; missing links use manual lookup. The director captures actual bar_reference, balance_issue and desired_marking in s3 at full time after performance.
Same-system annotation save has no time saving. No automatic musical direction, new score distribution or hidden communication action is proposed.
research_questions: Do existing score tools already jump directly between the marked passages and current parts?

incremental.description: Maintain current-part links and rehearsal bookmarks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only navigation changes: 10 times 30% = 3 hours less 0.5 upkeep = 2.5. Low halves navigation benefit: 1.5 minus 0.5 = 1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study scores in detail and develop musical interpretations.

steps.what: Find and compare passages in the current digital score using native bar navigation
inputs: existing bar numbers and movement markers

steps.what: Study the music in detail and develop interpretive choices
Write and check interpretive annotations against the score and intended musical effect
Save the approved final interpretive annotations

tasks.design: Configure native passage navigation and movement bookmarks in {DIGITAL_SCORE}, denoted OTHER. Study, interpretation and expressive annotation remain human work. Keep final annotation approval and same-system save separate, with no save benefit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Moving among related passages can interrupt score study.
tasks.enabler_now: Native score navigation reduces finding time while leaving the reading and interpretation intact.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding structure and choosing a convincing interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The director relates musical detail to a coherent expressive whole.
tasks.altitude: Human score interpretation with native navigation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bar and movement bookmarks can reduce retrieval effort in an existing digital score.

assumptions: All shares are provisional. Credit navigation only if it remains manual after current native tools; no reading or creative time is removed.

Publisher score supplies existing bar_number and movement markers. The director checks edition and correspondence in s1. Missing markers require manual navigation. s3 retains full capture of actual interpretive decisions and bar references.
No generated interpretation or new distribution is proposed. The annotation save stays fully retained.
research_questions: How much passage-finding effort remains after the current score tools native navigation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only navigation changes: 10 times 40% = 4 hours minus 0.5 upkeep = 3.5. Low halves this benefit: 2 minus 0.5 = 1.5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create musical and tonal structures using music theory.

steps.what: Invent and develop melodies, harmonies and tonal structures through musical judgement
Enter and copy chosen musical structures using native notation patterns and exact transposition
inputs: composer-entered pitches, durations, voices and transposition interval

steps.what: Listen, inspect and correct the notation against intended harmonies and melodies
outputs: approved final musical structures and notation

steps.what: Save the approved final musical structures in the notation project
inputs: approved final musical structures and notation

tasks.design: Use {NOTATION_SOFTWARE} native motif copying, duration patterns and exact transposition; OTHER denotes that tool. The composer supplies and chooses all musical material, enters initial notes, then hears and corrects the result. Same-system save earns no benefit. No model composes the structure.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated chosen motifs may be entered note by note despite exact repetition or transposition.
tasks.enabler_now: Native notation transformations can reproduce chosen material exactly.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing meaningful harmony, melody and overall form.
tasks.human_edge: The composer determines what the music should express and whether it works.
tasks.altitude: Creative music-making with exact notation operations.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: notation software can copy motifs and transpose exact pitches; this supports mechanical notation, not creative quality.

assumptions: Provisional effort shares assume residual repeated note entry after current native functions; existing shortcuts or playback runtime earn no saving.

Composer supplies pitch, duration, voice, motif_selection and interval in s1-s2. The 14 retained s2 hours count initial entry, selection and checking; absent exact input uses manual notation. s3 retains full musical and notation correction.
Only repeated entry is reduced, not creative generation or listening. Save remains fully retained.
unknowns: Current use of motif and transposition functions
research_questions: Which exact repeated motifs are still entered manually after the notation tools native functions?

incremental.description: Maintain notation shortcuts and verify pattern behaviour after updates

approvals.approved_version: s3 complete corrected musical structures and notation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only repeated notation entry changes: 20 times 30% = 6 hours minus 1 upkeep = 5. Low halves that benefit: 3 minus 1 = 2.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Human musical creation and direction supported by exact score tools.
reach: Less mechanical score navigation and repeated notation
skills_to_grow: Using native score bookmarks and exact notation transformations
role.ambitious_version: The director and composer spend less effort finding and repeating notes while retaining all musical interpretation and live direction.
